key_insight: UniX resolves the conflict between semantic understanding and pixel-level image generation by unifying autoregressive and diffusion paradigms in a single foundation model for chest X-rays, enabling strong performance on both report-level tasks and high-fidelity image synthesis.
problem_solved: Existing unified medical models sacrifice either semantic abstraction (understanding) or pixel-perfect reconstruction (generation) when using shared autoregressive architectures; UniX addresses this trade-off to support both tasks effectively.
method: Dual-path architecture that decouples semantic (autoregressive) and pixel-generation (diffusion) pathways while sharing a common visual backbone.
Task-specific heads and a hybrid training objective that jointly optimizes report-level understanding and image reconstruction without parameter interference.
Conditioned generation and disentangled latent representations to preserve clinical semantics in generated chest X-rays and reduce task conflict.
impact: UniX lets practitioners use one foundation model for both diagnostic understanding (reports, classification) and realistic image generation (augmentation, simulation), reducing deployment complexity and improving multi-task clinical workflows.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing shared backbone with two branches: autoregressive (understanding) and diffusion (generation).
Side-by-side examples: ground-truth X-ray, generated X-ray, and extracted report to illustrate fidelity and semantic alignment.
Trade-off / ablation chart comparing unified autoregressive-only, diffusion-only, and UniX on understanding vs generation metrics.
Pipeline flowchart showing training data (images + reports), hybrid loss components, and inference modes (understand vs generate).
paper_title: UniX: Unifying Autoregression and Diffusion for Chest X-Ray Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ruiheng Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Huangxuan Zhao, Hao Yan, Xiao He
